timing.scope: Fully resident fixed4x129prompt/64output,3repetitions after warmup; integrated stdio timings conservatively compared to default original public callback delivery times; not sustained-serving parity; original cross-process last-three-head variation is preserved separately

measurement: Primary original timing is the first predeclared three-run default reference. Product timing uses the new selected-kernel policy. Prefill is last first-token receipt after submission/release; decode is mean over four per-request(first-to-last delivered)/63, then median across runs. Product includes raw tokenizer/stdio/admission; original is pretokenized public engine callbacks. Diagnostic readbacks and kernel observers are outside all timed intervals.

policy_provenance.method: Selected original prefill normalization launch configurations and compiled PTX; no fitting to logits. Six input-layer reduction modes differ from eager46. All post-attention modes unchanged.
policy_provenance.decode: Graph replay bypasses Python kernel observer; product comparison against all recorded complete decode heads independently checks the selected policy.

qualification_limits: Observed gates apply only to this pinned checkpoint, GPU, context and four129-token prompts with64 outputs.
Original default versus eager outputs differ. Both profiles remain separate and all previous golds are preserved.

Two original default processes agree on tokens and253heads but differ on final three request0 heads under identical recorded logical geometry. Product matches256/256 of the kernel-recorded original capture in normal and ASAN builds, and253/256 of the first capture. This does not establish universally repeatable original logits; cause remains unresolved.
Timings are sequential warmed runs on unlocked clocks, without interleaved thermal-drift control.
This is not a matched sustained-serving comparison or offloaded-model benchmark. Prior local SLO evidence belongs to the earlier explicit eager profile.
All-family release, broader resident/offload workloads, transfer/stall/peak qualification, capability matrix and CPU/Metal coverage remain active goal work.
